scope: Holistic source-locked architectural-clay review of the delivered texture-free GLB, its 23 renders and 4 phone boards against the three locked references for london_crescent_terrace / london-crescent-terrace-bath-stone (variant 0, Bath Stone Grand), with read-only measurement of the whole GLB, my own renders of it, a check of each of the builder's six claimed changes, and a re-test of all eleven findings of my v005 review. decision_note: No P0, no P1, ten P2. Both v005 blockers are fixed and I could measure each fix: the coupled corner columns now stand apart with wall between them, a capital and a pedestal each, and nothing of one column inside another; and the railing bars run round every corner. The roof is single-skinned and the whole model is an exact mirror image. Narrowing the bays to make room for the corner pairs caused no collision. I re-ran every geometric check on the whole model and added section tests; they found one hidden gap (no floor in the door reveals) and one hairline (the corner columns barely touch the wall), both recorded as P2 with my reasons. This pass says the model is a complete, coherent building that follows the street view and the oblique. It does not say the source set is sound: the roof-plan reference shows a different building, and a person must rule on that before any activation. It is not keeper approval, and runtime integration is untested.

findings.title: The four corner columns touch the wall only at its arris, and near the top the tapering shaft stands clear of it, leaving a hairline of daylight from one raking direction
evidence: GLB: the axis of each outer corner column (60.887, -0.400 and its mirror) is 0.316 m from the nearest point of the upper wall, which is the wall's corner arris; at the inner corners (47.887, -0.400) it is 0.306 m. The shaft radius is 0.330 m at the base and 0.282 m at the neck. So the shaft is into the arris by 14 mm (outer) and 24 mm (inner) at the foot, meets it at about 8.4 m (outer) and 9.4 m (inner), and stands clear above that, by 33 mm (outer) and 23 mm (inner) at 11.0 m. Every other column is 0.220 m from a flat wall face and stays engaged by 110 mm at the foot and 62 mm at the neck.

My own renders of the GLB with a magenta background: myrenders/slit_outer_right_top.png (telephoto along the gap: a clear strip of background between shaft and wall at 10.6 m; none at 6.0 m) and myrenders/slit_eye_convex.png (eye level, about 11 m from the outer corner on the convex side, 50 degree lens, 1600x1200: a line of background 1 to 3 px wide over 155 rows between the corner column and the wall).
Not visible in any of the builder's 23 renders, including renders/corner_close.png, outer_corner_close.png and corner_eye.png, none of which looks along that line.
prework-manifest.json describes the columns as three-quarters engaged.
findings.why_p2: The wall behind is closed and the column stands on its plinth under the corner of the entablature, so nothing is unsupported and nothing opens the envelope. It is a hairline, seen only close up and only within a few degrees of one direction at each corner. It became possible in this version because the partners no longer overlap the corner column.
findings.required_action: Carry a short return of wall, or a square pier, behind each corner column so the shaft stays into masonry for its whole height; then look along the tangent at 10 m height in a close view.

findings.title: Small misfits remain at the corners: the corner capital shows its roll side to the end elevation, and the corner pedestal stands 31 to 39 mm proud of the coping with its hollow top open in that strip
evidence: GLB: each corner column carries an ordinary capital turned to the long side. Its two rolls run along X (plan angles 1.8 and 178.2 degrees) at Z -0.103 and -0.697, at all four corners, and mirror exactly. The capital therefore faces the convex side at the outer corners and the concave front at the inner corners, and shows a roll side to the end elevation.

renders/end_contact.png at about x 315-385, y 262-300 and x 1215-1285, y 262-300: the first and last of the nine capitals on the end elevation show a plain horizontal cylinder where the other seven show two scroll faces. renders/corner_close.png at about x 825-910, y 600-630 and renders/outer_corner_close.png at about x 690-775, y 540-575 show the long roll of the corner capital from the corner.

GLB: the corner pedestal of the balustrade is 0.557 m square, X 60.660 to 61.217 and Z -0.629 to -0.072 at the outer right corner, against a coping that ends at X 61.186 and Z -0.110. It projects 31 mm and 39 mm beyond the coping. The pedestal is a box with no top, so in that L-shaped strip a ray from above passes inside it and first meets the cornice at 13.00 m. The same at the other three corners.
My own render myrenders/R_outer_parapet.png: the inside faces of the corner pedestal show along its top edge (532 px at 1400x1050 from 8 m). Not resolved in any builder render.
findings.why_p2: Turning the corner capital to the long front is the plain, honest way to handle a two-faced capital at a corner, it is applied by one mirrored rule, and it reads as intended. A capital with an angled corner scroll would be the classical refinement. The pedestal strip is 3 to 4 cm wide and the material is double-sided, so it shades as stone.
findings.required_action: Either accept the turned capital or give the four corner columns a capital with scroll faces on both outer sides. Trim the corner pedestal to the coping line or give the pedestals tops.

findings.title: There is no floor in the thickness of the wall behind any of the 36 doors
evidence: GLB: behind each door leaf a vertical ray from 1.0 m finds no surface at all from 0.04 m to 0.62 m behind the leaf, across the door width. The room floor starts at the inner wall face. All 36 doors.

Found by flood-filling vertical sections from outside at 1 cm: on planes X = 3.40 and X = 20.00, which pass through a front door and a garden door, the ground-floor room is reached from beneath, under the door leaf (myrenders/section_x3.40.png). On eight other X planes and three Z planes, and on 13 plan sections from 0.5 to 12.4 m at 2 cm, no room or roof void is reached. With glass, doors and joinery removed the same test leaks, as it should.

Not visible from outside: the leaves are opaque and closed, and of 900 rays sent in through the 36 door lights at 35 to 75 degrees below the horizontal, every one lands on a floor, a wall or a ceiling.
The same strip is missing in v005. I did not run a section test on v005 and did not find it then.

reference_observations.street_view: variant_0.png, 1024x768, opened whole again for this review. Eye level inside the crescent near one end, looking along the concave front. Plain ashlar ground storey with one sash to a bay and a white door about every third bay; a band; unfluted three-quarter Ionic columns through two storeys; one tall and one shorter sash to a bay, both plain one over one, in thin stone surrounds with wall showing beside them; an iron guard between the plinths at each first-floor window; a plain frieze and a modillion cornice; a balustrade with a pedestal over each column; broad stone stacks with a row of pots; slate and a hip at the far end, where two columns stand close together with a gap between them. Continuous iron railings at the pavement edge.
reference_observations.oblique: variant_0_angle_60.jpg, 1195x896, opened whole again. High, from outside one end. A half ellipse opening to a lawn. Near end: six window bays and nine columns, coupled at both corners with a gap between each pair; a white door under the third window from the concave corner, over a railed sunken area with steps; a basement storey. The convex side carries the same order at close spacing, with doors and areas. Roof: slate ranges, a stone upstand and a broad stack at each party wall, small lead dormers behind the balustrade including about four on the end slope, one clean hip over the near end, lead-covered boxes between the ranges.
reference_observations.roof_plan: variant_0_angle_90.jpg, 1195x896, opened whole again. A different building: a short block of nine or ten houses between two round lawns, concave on both long sides, with flared hipped ends and deep wells between the ranges.
reference_observations.departures_of_the_model: From the street view: glazing bars where it shows none (declared); no ashlar joints (declared); no sunken areas (declared); otherwise storeys, order, guards, entablature, balustrade, stacks, railings and window proportions agree, and the fitted view lays over the reference closely. From the oblique: no areas, bridges or basement storey (declared); no lead boxes on the roof (declared); convex bays too wide near the ends (declared as built, P2-05); end-bay windows wider in their bays than the reference shows (not declared, P2-03); two dormers on the end slope for about four (P2-06). The coupled corner columns and the railings now agree with both perspective references. From the roof plan: everything about the plan (declared).

positive_observations: The model hash and byte count I computed match the build report and the delivery record, the three reference hashes match the manifest, and the four boards carry the model hash prefix 705fc02b21d5.

GLB: 12 nodes, 12 meshes, 12 materials, one per clay role; no images, textures, samplers, cameras, animations or skins; no node transforms; 170,276 triangles; bounds 126.317 by 19.160 by 48.400 m; lowest geometry 0.000 m; every node carries the archetype and variant ids.

Triangle winding agrees with the stored normal at all 510,828 triangle corners; normals are unit length; no zero-area triangle. None of the 1,504 closed solids is inside out, and every open stone, dressed-stone, slate, lead and pot shell faces outward.

All six builder claims check out against the GLB. The corner columns stand clear; the railing bars run round every corner; the roof and every other part mirror; the party-wall upstands start inside the ceiling slab; the two new views exist; the knobs are on the centre stile.

Nothing collides at the corners or in the end bays after the bays were narrowed (front 2.27 to 2.30 m, ends 1.858 m): glass, frames, sills, surrounds and guards are all clear of shafts, bases and plinths.

The envelope is closed: flood-filled from outside, 13 plan sections and 13 vertical sections reach no room and no roof void, except from beneath through the door reveals (P2-04). From 72 outside viewpoints no interior or floor surface is the first thing seen.

The roof is closed and single-skinned everywhere; all 34 stacks are bedded at least 0.44 m into the slopes on every side; all 238 pots stand on their caps; nothing floats (of 14,732 separate parts none is more than 8 mm from its neighbour).
Every wall opening is a real section with a room behind it: 324 windows, 36 door lights and 36 doors, each door 1.01 m wide with a 35 mm threshold and a clear stone path through the railings.
The whole model is an exact mirror image about its middle, tested at vertex and at surface level.
All fourteen mandatory views and nine more are present; the eight whole-building views have at least 99 px of clear margin on every side; the boards are 1080x1920 and state the known differences.
Controls: the same roof, mirror and support tests run on v005 reproduce its known faults, so their absence here is a real difference.
for_human_acceptance: The catalogue roof-plan image shows a different building. Accept in writing that the street view and the oblique are the plan authority for this variant, or replace that image, before any activation (P2-10; method Gate A and profile condition 1).
Eighteen houses and 54 front bays is an estimate from a partly hidden view; my range is 49 to 57 bays.
The model is one fixed object, 126.32 by 48.40 by 19.16 m, where the catalogue lists a 6 m by 12 m plot. It cannot be scaled or repeated under the method.
No sunken areas, bridges, steps or basement storey, although two of the three references show them.
Six-over-six sashes throughout although the street thumbnail shows plain sashes.
The convex side carries the giant order with bays widening from 2.68 m to 3.96 m and an inferred garden door to each house (P2-05).
Corner capitals are ordinary capitals turned to the long front, so the end elevations show a roll at each extremity (P2-02); end-bay windows sit tight between the columns (P2-03).
Dormers are surface features with no attic; interiors are schematic; there is no floor in the door reveals (P2-04), which matters only if something is to pass through a doorway.
The catalogue text (114 columns, thirty or more houses, rusticated base) does not describe what is built.
Texture-free clay, every material double-sided, glass blended with the transmission extension, 170,276 triangles: whether that is acceptable for the runtime.
This review grants nothing. Keeper approval, runtime activation and publication are a person's to give, and runtime integration is untested.
limitations: I am an AI reviewer, and the same one that reviewed v005 earlier in this session. I have no builder context and did not open the generator, but this is not a fresh pair of eyes on v005's ground: anything I misjudged then I may have misjudged again. One thing I missed in v005, the floor in the door reveals, I found only now.

I worked from stills, from ray, raster and section tests I wrote for these reviews, and from my own flat-shaded renders of the GLB. I did not see the model in a real-time viewer or a moving camera, so flicker, depth precision and the blended, transmissive glass are not assessed.

I did not open, list or run anything under tools/catalogue_crescent_terrace_pilot or tools/catalogue_plus15_concrete_pilot, so I did not check the generator, the camera file, the triangle budget or the claim that the model rebuilds to the same bytes. I could not confirm that the renders were made from a reimport of this exact file; the details that changed in this version (separate corner columns, bars round the corners, clean hips) are in both the renders and the GLB.
Runtime integration is not tested: placement, terrain, entrance routes, the fixed-scale contract and the catalogue record were not examined.

The references are generated images that do not agree with each other and carry no scale. My pixel readings are good to about 3 px; the house count, the convex-side spacing and the width of the end windows in the oblique are estimates.

Sampling is finite: 5 cm from above over the whole plan and 2 cm over the ends, corners and middle; 72 orthographic views at 4.6 cm per pixel from outside; 63 rays on the normal and 54 slanted rays to each wall pane; sections at 1 and 2 cm on 26 planes; coplanar faces within 2 mm. A smaller defect, or one between my section planes, could be missed.
The severity of every finding is my judgement. I looked for a reason to hold any of them at P1 and did not find one I could defend, but P2-01 and P2-03 are the two a stricter reader might raise.
I did not open v001, v003 or v004, and used no git command. I used the v005 GLB only as a control.
Evidence paths beginning myrenders/ or crops/ are my own working images in the reviewer's scratch folder and may not outlive this session.
